# Sapwood - Complete AI Reference

> Shape your signer -- browser-based local and remote management UI for the Heartwood ESP32 signing device.

Repository: https://github.com/forgesworn/sapwood
Live: https://sapwood.forgesworn.dev/
Licence: MIT

---

## What it is

Sapwood is a static single-page application (SPA) that manages a Heartwood ESP32 hardware signer. Bootstrap over USB (no install, no server), then leave the device online in WiFi-standalone mode and manage it remotely from Sapwood on a phone through Nostr relays.

Stack: Svelte 5 (runes mode), Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest.

---

## Architecture

```
Browser (Sapwood)  --Web Serial-->  Heartwood               (local, USB)
Phone (Sapwood)    --Nostr relays--> Heartwood outbound WiFi (remote)
```

Local USB management speaks the Heartwood frame protocol directly over the serial connection: no bridge, no server, no network path from the device to the internet.

Remote management sends authenticated, NIP-44-encrypted management events (kind 24134) over Nostr relays to the device's outbound WiFi connection; `src/lib/relay-transport.ts` runs one persistent subscription and routes replies back to pending requests by id, mirroring bray's management probe. The device exposes no inbound port and requires no cloud account.

A separate heartwood bridge daemon (in heartwood-esp32) exists for the hardened USB-only tier, where the signing chip's radio stays off and an always-on host relays NIP-46 signing traffic over the cable. `src/lib/bridge-probe.ts` detects whether an origin is actually serving that bridge API, so a static host answering with the SPA's own `index.html` is not mistaken for one.

---

## Source layout

```
src/lib/
  frame.ts            -- TypeScript port of heartwood-common/src/frame.rs (encode/decode)
  frame-stream.ts      -- splits the serial byte stream into log lines and frames
  serial.ts            -- Web Serial API transport
  relay-transport.ts   -- Nostr relay management transport (kind 24134, NIP-44)
  bridge-probe.ts       -- detects a real heartwood bridge API vs a static-host 404 page
  bridge-setup.ts       -- bridge secret / session setup helpers
  device.svelte.ts      -- Svelte 5 reactive device state store
  crc32.ts              -- CRC32-IEEE 802.3 implementation
  types.ts              -- shared TypeScript types (MasterInfo, ClientPolicy, OtaStatus, etc.)
  kinds.ts              -- Nostr event kind labels and risk categories, used by the permission UI
  op-mgmt.ts            -- operator-key management authority for remote requests
  operator-key.ts        -- operator key derivation, shared with the CLI
  backup.ts              -- backup/restore engine and encrypted envelope (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305)
  provision.ts            -- master-slot provisioning helpers
  ota.ts                  -- OTA upload/verify flow
  flasher.ts               -- app-only USB flashing for single-slot boards
  recovery.ts               -- family recovery (words-only rebuild) flow
  pacing.ts                  -- UART write pacing, shared with the CLI
```

`cli/` mirrors the same operations as a cross-platform CLI over node-serialport: `cli/transport.ts` for the transport, `cli/commands.ts` for the commands (pure, tested against a fake transport).

---

## Frame protocol

TypeScript port of the Rust implementation in heartwood-common/src/frame.rs, defined in `src/lib/frame.ts` as `FrameType`.

### Wire format

```
[0x48 0x57] [type_u8] [length_u16_be] [payload...] [crc32_be32]
```

- Magic: 2 bytes `0x48 0x57` ("HW")
- Type: 1 byte frame type
- Length: 2 bytes big-endian, payload byte count
- Payload: 0-N bytes (type-dependent)
- CRC32: 4 bytes big-endian, IEEE 802.3 polynomial, covers type + length + payload bytes

### Frame types in active use

| Frame | Type | Direction | Payload |
|-------|------|-----------|---------|
| PROVISION_LIST | 0x05 | host -> device | (empty) |
| PROVISION_LIST_RESPONSE | 0x07 | device -> host | JSON masters, then derived personas with `persona: true` |
| PROVISION_REMOVE | 0x04 | host -> device | slot_u8; device ACKs then reboots, remaining slots renumber |
| DERIVE_IDENTITY | 0x60 | host -> device | parent_slot (1 byte) + name (utf8); device derives the nsec-tree child on-device |
| DERIVE_IDENTITY_RESPONSE | 0x61 | device -> host | JSON `{slot, label, npub, parent_slot, purpose, existing}` |
| ENCRYPTED_REQUEST | 0x10 | host -> device | target_pubkey (32) + client_pubkey (32) + created_at (8, u64 be) + NIP-44 ciphertext (base64); a full NIP-46 request |
| SIGN_ENVELOPE_RESPONSE | 0x35 | device -> host | signed kind:24133 envelope; content decrypts under the client-identity conversation key |
| SESSION_AUTH | 0x21 | host -> device | 32-byte bridge secret; device replies SESSION_ACK (0x22) |
| CONNSLOT_LIST | 0x42 | host -> device | master_slot (1 byte); secrets redacted, no session needed |
| CONNSLOT_REVOKE | 0x46 | host -> device | master_slot (1) + slot_index (1); requires SESSION_AUTH first |
| FACTORY_RESET | 0x24 | host -> device | (empty, requires button) |
| OTA_BEGIN | 0x30 | host -> device | size_u32_be (4 bytes) + sha256_hex (64 bytes); requires button |
| OTA_CHUNK | 0x31 | host -> device | offset_u32_be (4 bytes) + binary chunk |
| OTA_FINISH | 0x32 | host -> device | (empty) |
| OTA_STATUS | 0x33 | device -> host | status_byte (0 = ok) |
| BACKUP_EXPORT_REQUEST | 0x50 | host -> device | (empty, requires button; device replies with JSON `BackupPayload`) |
| BACKUP_EXPORT_RESPONSE | 0x51 | device -> host | JSON `BackupPayload` (masters + connection slots + bridge secret) |
| BACKUP_IMPORT_REQUEST | 0x52 | host -> device | JSON `BackupPayload`, masters pre-filtered to those the device holds; requires button |
| BACKUP_IMPORT_RESPONSE | 0x53 | device -> host | 1 byte: 0x01 ok / 0x00 fail |

**Declared but not implemented.** `POLICY_LIST_REQUEST` (0x27), `POLICY_LIST_RESPONSE` (0x28), `POLICY_REVOKE` (0x29) and `POLICY_UPDATE` (0x2A) exist in `heartwood-common/src/types.rs` and in `frame.ts`, but the firmware has no handler for any of them; Sapwood only touches them in byte-roundtrip tests. App permissions go over the `CONNSLOT_*` frames instead.

### Stream parsing

The serial stream carries both ESP-IDF log lines (plain text, newline-terminated) and protocol frames (binary). `frame-stream.ts` hunts for the `0x48 0x57` magic sequence to separate them; `serial.ts` wraps the Web Serial API around it and emits frame and log events.

---

## Features

### Identities (masters)

Lists provisioned master slots on the device: slot index, npub, derivation mode. Calls PROVISION_LIST (0x05), receives PROVISION_LIST_RESPONSE (0x07). New identities can be typed by name and derived on-device (DERIVE_IDENTITY, no secret in the browser), or imported from a phrase/nsec/ncryptsec for older firmware.

### Apps (connected clients)

One surface across USB, WiFi and bridge transports for creating connections and setting per-kind signing permissions. Uses the `CONNSLOT_*` frames (list, create, update, revoke, uri) rather than the unimplemented `POLICY_*` frames.

### Firmware OTA

Uploads a firmware binary to the device over USB. Steps: select a `.bin` file, SHA-256 computed in-browser; OTA_BEGIN (0x30) sent with size and hash, device prompts for a button press; binary split into chunks sent as OTA_CHUNK (0x31); OTA_FINISH (0x32) sent, device verifies the hash and reboots; a progress bar tracks chunk offset. OTA_STATUS (0x33) responses are checked throughout. Boards without an OTA slot (T-Display, C6, an early V4) get a quick app-only USB update instead: `planAppOnlyWrite` in `flasher.ts` reads the partition table off the chip and refuses a two-slot board before writing.

### Backup and restore

Backs up app pairings and the bridge secret to an encrypted file (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305), USB only, button-confirmed (BACKUP_EXPORT_REQUEST/RESPONSE, BACKUP_IMPORT_REQUEST/RESPONSE). Separately, typed 19/31-word identity recovery, the operator key, and re-derivable named identities each have their own backup path; see docs/backup-and-restore.md and docs/key-backup.md.

### Logs

Streams real-time ESP-IDF log output from the device.

### Factory reset

Erases all keys and client policies. Sends FACTORY_RESET (0x24); the device will not execute it until the physical button is pressed.

---

## Security model

**Secrets never leave the ESP32.** The protocol only carries public keys and npubs, policy/connection metadata, NIP-44 ciphertext and signatures (not plaintext key material), and firmware binary chunks (OTA).

**Physical button confirmation** gates every destructive or secret-revealing operation: factory reset, OTA, backup export/import, and provisioning. A compromised Sapwood SPA cannot extract keys or perform destructive actions without physical access to the button.

**Network tiers:**
- WiFi-standalone (standard): the signer joins WiFi and serves management and NIP-46 over relays itself. This is what the guided flasher produces by default.
- USB-only, radio off (hardened): no network stack runs on the key-holding chip; remote signing requires the heartwood bridge daemon on an always-on host with the signer plugged in.

Regardless of tier, firmware updates, factory reset and PIN changes always require the USB cable. Identity management works over WiFi too: derive-by-name sends no secret at all, and importing a phrase/nsec/ncryptsec travels NIP-44 encrypted end-to-end under the operator-signer conversation key, so relays only ever carry ciphertext.

**Planned: Web Bluetooth (portable mode only).** BLE connectivity is planned for child-key-only portable mode. Before it ships: rate limiting on management frame types, button-press BLE pairing, and CSP headers on static hosting.

## Dependencies

Runtime (compiled into bundle): `@noble/ciphers`, `@noble/curves`, `@noble/hashes`, `@paulmillr/qr`, `@scure/bip32`, `@scure/bip39`, `esptool-js`, `nostr-tools`, `serialport` (CLI only).

Dev: `svelte`, `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte`, `vite`, `typescript`, `vitest`, `jsdom`, `@testing-library/svelte`, `@playwright/test`, `esbuild`.

See package.json for exact ranges.

---

## Build commands

```bash
npm install           # install dependencies
npm run dev            # dev server at http://localhost:5173
npm run build           # production build to dist/
npm run build:cli        # bundle the CLI to dist-cli/sapwood.mjs
npm run preview           # preview dist/ locally
npm run check              # svelte-check
npm run check:cli           # tsc on the CLI
npm test                     # run all tests (vitest run)
npm run test:watch            # watch mode
npm run test:e2e               # playwright end-to-end tests
```

---

## Browser support

Web Serial API is required.

| Browser | Minimum version |
|---------|----------------|
| Chrome | 89+ |
| Edge | 89+ |
| Opera | 76+ |
| Firefox | Not supported |
| Safari | Not supported |

---

## Conventions

- British English in all prose, comments, and UI copy
- ESM-only (`"type": "module"`, target ES2022)
- Monospace font throughout (terminal/cockpit aesthetic)
- Dark theme only
- Tone: sovereign, precise, calm. No exclamation marks.
- No em dashes in UI copy: use a full stop, comma or colon instead
- Git commits: `type: description` format. No Co-Authored-By lines.

---

## Ecosystem

| Component | Repo | Role |
|-----------|------|------|
| Heartwood | forgesworn/heartwood-esp32 | ESP32 firmware, bridge, provision CLI |
| Sapwood | forgesworn/sapwood | Web management UI (this repo) |
| Bark | see README | Browser extension for NIP-46 signing |
| nsec-tree | see README | Key derivation library |

Named after the living, active layer of wood between bark and heartwood.
